OVER: Copy the second item to the top.
ROT: ( a b c -- b c a )
Bring the third item to the top.
?DUP: Copy the top item if it is not zero.
TUCK: Copy the top item below the second.
2DUP: ( a b -- a b a b )
2SWAP: ( a b c d -- c d a b )
2OVER: ( a b c d -- a b c d a b )
Copy the second pair to the top.
DEPTH: Number of items on the data stack (before n).
MOD: Remainder of n1 / n2 (sign of n1).
*/: n1 * n2 / n3, with a 64-bit middle result (no overflow).
2/: Shift right one bit, keeping the sign.
LSHIFT: Shift x left by u bits.  1 5 LSHIFT gives 32.
RSHIFT: Shift x right by u bits, zeros in at the top.
M*: Signed multiply to a double-cell result.
UM*: Unsigned multiply to a double-cell result.
FM/MOD: Signed double divide, quotient rounded toward minus infinity.
SM/REM: Signed double divide, quotient rounded toward zero.
S>D: Widen a cell to a double cell.
@: Fetch the 32-bit cell at a. Works on any address, registers too.
!: Store x in the 32-bit cell at a.
+!: Add n to the cell at a.
2@: Fetch two cells: x2 from a, x1 from a+4.
2!: Store two cells: x2 at a, x1 at a+4.
,: Append a cell to the dictionary.
C,: Append a byte to the dictionary.
ALLOT: Reserve n bytes of dictionary space.
ALIGN: Align HERE to a cell boundary.
ALIGNED: Round an address up to a cell boundary.
COUNT: Turn a counted string into address and length.
FILL: Set u bytes from a to c.
MOVE: Copy u bytes from a1 to a2 (overlap safe).
TRUE: The true flag: all bits set.
STATE: Address of STATE: non-zero while compiling a definition.
BASE: Address of the number base used for input and output.
>IN: Address of the offset into the current input line.
KEY: Wait for one character from the console.
ACCEPT: Read a line of at most n characters into a.
Print a signed number and a space.
Print an unsigned number and a space.
<#: Start building a number's text (pictured output).
#: Add the next digit to the number's text.
HOLD: Add a character to the number's text.
SIGN: Add a minus sign if n is negative.
>NUMBER: ( ud a u -- ud' a' u' )
Convert digits from text; stops at the first non-digit.
WORD: Parse a word delimited by c; counted string.
CHAR: The first character of the next word.  CHAR A gives 65.
[CHAR]: Compile: as CHAR, inside a definition.
(: Comment up to ). Used for stack comments.
\\: Comment to the end of the line.
.(: Print text up to ), at once, even inside a definition.
FIND: Look up a counted-string name: 1 immediate, -1 normal.
': The execution token of the next word.
[']: Compile: as ', inside a definition.  ['] TICK 0 IRQ!
EVALUATE: Interpret the text a u as if typed.
QUIT: Empty the return stack and return to the console.
ABORT: Empty both stacks and return to the console (error -1).
ABORT\": Compile: if f is true when run, print text and ABORT (-2).
ENVIRONMENT?: Environment queries: none are answered here.
[: Stop compiling: interpret the rest, inside a definition.
:: Start a definition: name, then words, then ;
CREATE: Make a word that pushes the address of the space after it.
DOES>: Give the newest CREATEd word an action: the code after DOES>.
VARIABLE: Make a cell variable; name pushes its address.
CONSTANT: Make a word that pushes x.
IMMEDIATE: Make the newest word run even while compiling.
>BODY: The data address of a CREATEd word.
LITERAL: Compile: push x when the definition runs.
POSTPONE: Compile: compile the next word's behaviour into this one.
RECURSE: Compile a call to the word being defined.
IF: Run the following code only if f is true:  f IF ... THEN
ELSE: The other branch:  f IF ... ELSE ... THEN
BEGIN: Start of a loop: BEGIN ... f UNTIL, BEGIN ... AGAIN, BEGIN ... f WHILE ... REPEAT
UNTIL: Go back to BEGIN until f is true.
AGAIN: Go back to BEGIN for ever.
WHILE: Leave the BEGIN loop when f is false.
REPEAT: Go back to BEGIN (end of a WHILE loop).
DO: Counted loop:  10 0 DO ... LOOP  runs with I = 0 .. 9.
LOOP: Add 1 to the index; loop until it reaches the limit.
+LOOP: Add n to the index; loop until it crosses the limit.
I: The index of the innermost DO loop.
J: The index of the next outer DO loop.
UNLOOP: Drop the loop's control, before EXIT from inside a DO loop.
>R: Move x to the return stack.
R>: Move x back from the return stack.
R@: Copy the top of the return stack.
.\": Compile: print the text up to " when the word runs.
S\": The text up to " as address and length.
SAVE: Copy the dictionary to flash; it is restored at every boot.
EMPTY: Erase the saved dictionary and clear the RAM one.
IRQ!: Run xt on interrupt n and enable it; 0 n IRQ! disables it.
